The electric conductivity of the ZnF 2 −AlF 3 −PbF 3 −LiF glasses decreases with increasing LiF content, which results from F − ion trapping by Li + ions; and the value of the decupling parameter decreases with increasing Li + ion content.
the electric conductivity of Zn F 2 −AlF 3 −PbF 3 −LiF glasses decreases with an increase of LiF content, which results from a reduction of F − ion mobility due to the trapping of F ions by Li ions.
The electrical conductivity of ZnF2–PbF–LiF–AlF3 glasses decreases with the increase of LiF content, and the stretching exponent of the conductivity relaxation is small for the present glasses.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the electrical properties of the ZnF 2 −AlF 3 −PbF 3 −LiF glass system.
the electrical properties of the ZnF 2 -AlF 3 -PbF 3 glasses.
the synthesis, structure, electrical conductivity, and relaxation of ZnF 3 –AlF 2 –PbF −LiF glasses.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the electric conductivity and relaxation of the present glasses are consistent with the model proposed by Ngai and co-workers.
there is no single mechanism which can explain the conductivity of the present glasses.
the present results are consistent with the model of a continuous distribution of relaxation times, which is also consistent with the observed conductivity relaxation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the conductivity and the relaxation in the ZnF 2–AlF 3–Pb F 2–LiF glass system are strongly influenced by the Li + ions, as well as by the AlF 3 and PbF 2 components.
the present glasses have the characteristics of a supercooled liquid and not of a glass.
the conductivity is controlled by the Li + ions, while the stretching exponent is determined by the Al 3+ ions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the conductivity of ZnF2–PbF 1–2–AlF 3–xLiF x glass is controlled by the presence of F− ions, which act as the charge carriers.
the relaxation time τ is not a single-valued function of the electric field strength.

the electric relaxation is a superposition of two processes, namely, the Johari-Goldstein process, which is independent of the composition, and the β-relaxation process that is dependent on composition.
